pages.title: Skills, Plugins, and Extension UI
pages.purpose: Skills search/install, plugin package management, the plugin worker, and the extension UI bridge for the desktop renderer.
instructions: Explain plugin lifecycle actions and how npm/git toolchain resolution is required.
Explain skills search via skills.sh API with npx fallback and isolated cache retry.
Explain the extension UI request/response bridge, custom UI, and unsupported terminal-only features.

pages.title: Models, Auth, and Credentials
pages.purpose: Model provider configuration, models.json, OAuth login, API keys, credential synchronization, and the channel credential vault.
instructions: Document models.json read/write with optimistic concurrency and atomic writes.
Explain OAuth login flow and credential synchronization/recovery.
Explain model listing, refresh, preferences, and the model catalog.
Explain the OS credential vault (safeStorage) for channel secrets and its key validation.

pages.title: Agent Sessions, Files, and History
pages.purpose: How the Agent Host wraps pi-coding-agent sessions: session registry, indexing, history pagination, auto titles, file access roots, worktrees, and file watching.
instructions: Document AgentSessionWrapper lifecycle, command dispatch, queued turns, idle eviction, and dispose.
Explain file access roots, allowed roots caching, and worktree operations.
Explain the channels integration surface (runExternalTurn/runExternalCommand).
Explain the session index and watcher, history paging/cursors, and auto title generation.

pages.title: IPC and RPC Contract
pages.purpose: Typed MessagePort RPC layer: wire protocol, Api/Streams contract, client/server implementations, Main-Host parent RPC, and preload bridge.
instructions: Document IPC trust enforcement (isTrustedDesktopIpcSender) and how to add a new Api method.
Document the five wire message kinds and the subscribe/event model.
Explain how Renderer gets a port (preload postMessage transfer) and how Main issues one-shot Host RPCs.
Explain the lease mechanism on the RPC server.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Three-process Electron architecture: Main, Agent Host utilityProcess, sandboxed Renderer, plus the shared/contract layers and cross-process data/control flow.
instructions: Describe the primary data and control flows including Host crash/restart supervision.
Describe the security posture: sandbox, contextIsolation, CSP, typed IPC.
Explain responsibility and ownership boundaries for Main, Agent Host, Renderer, Preload, and the shared/contract modules.
Use the README architecture mermaid as a starting point but ground claims in source.

pages.title: WeChat, Telegram, and Feishu/Lark Adapters
pages.purpose: The three channel adapters: long-polling vs WebSocket transports, interactive login, rich rendering, and media handling differences.
instructions: Document the ChannelAdapter interface contract and each adapter's transport, reconnection, and login flow.
Explain media download/staging and outbound attachment delivery differences.
Explain rich/streaming rendering (Feishu Cards, Telegram streaming preview) and reaction states.
Highlight security-relevant differences (weixin context tokens, secret redaction).

pages.title: Messaging Channels Architecture
pages.purpose: Channel core: account lifecycle, adapters registry, inbound policy, pairing, bindings, per-session tool permissions, media staging, and outbound delivery.
instructions: Explain account connect/login/probe flows, channel runtime start/stop, and reconnection status.
Explain inbound policy evaluation (pairing/allowlist/open, groups, mention), bindings, and tool permission propagation.
Explain media staging, delivery receipts, and activity logging.
Explain slash commands and the PiSessionBridge external turn integration.

pages.title: Focused Change Guides
pages.purpose: Representative maintenance workflows: adding an Api method end-to-end, adding a Browser tool, adding a toolchain component, adding a channel adapter, and debugging a Host crash.
instructions: For each guide include the touchpoints, verification commands, and test expectations.
Give concrete step-by-step recipes grounded in the actual files and tests.
Include a debugging guide for Host crashes and diagnostics export.

pages.title: Testing and Quality Gates
pages.purpose: How the repository is tested and gated: node:test runner, contract coverage checks, security invariants, smoke tests, browser E2E, managed-process tests, and the verify pipeline.
instructions: Document the test matrix, how tests are discovered/run, and the CI platform matrix.
Explain how to run a single test file and how to add a new contract check.
Explain smoke, browser-electron, browser-agent-e2e, managed-process workflows/flood, and Windows helper tests.
Explain the verify pipeline order and the purpose of each check script.

pages.title: Advanced Browser Mode
pages.purpose: The opt-in Advanced Browser Mode: CDP command surface, network capture/replay, header rules, JavaScript experience store, secret vault, and fail-closed cookie gate.
instructions: Document CDP method allowlist, network body capture/replay confirmation, header rules and secret references.
Document the fail-closed cookie gate (SENSITIVE_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE) and its rationale.
Explain how Advanced Browser Mode is enabled (confirmation proof, settings gate).
Explain the identity management (UA/Client Hints) layering.

pages.title: Built-in Browser Service
pages.purpose: Main-owned WebContentsView browser: tabs, profiles, per-session authorization (persistent vs runtime grants), network policy, downloads, permissions, and tab restoration.
instructions: Explain network policy, private-network protection, downloads, uploads, external protocols, and certificate handling.
Explain permission levels (none/read/interact/advanced), persistent vs runtime grants, leases, and authorization requests.
Explain tab restoration persistence and the Browser Host RPC surface dispatched by BrowserService.

pages.title: Agent Host Supervision and Recovery
pages.purpose: How Main supervises the Agent Host utilityProcess: spawn, heartbeat liveness, crash restart budget, toolchain/browser snapshot ack, and packaged startup validation.
instructions: Document restart budget (CRASH_WINDOW_MS, MAX_RESTARTS), ping/pong heartbeat, and crash exit paths.
Explain packaged-startup validation and host-install recovery.
Explain toolchain/browser snapshot init/ack flow and owner identity for managed processes.

pages.title: Updates and Distribution Packaging
pages.purpose: electron-updater integration, update manager state machine, platform gating, and the electron-builder packaging/release pipeline including bundled toolchains and the Windows helper.
instructions: Describe the verify-before-pack quality gate.
Document update phases, download watchdog, install gating on active sessions, and error redaction.
Explain electron-builder files/extraResources layout, Windows NSIS, macOS dmg/zip, Linux AppImage, and the publish provider.

pages.title: Window, Tray, and App Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Main-process window lifecycle, single-instance lock, deep links, tray/badge, menus, renderer crash recovery, and window-state persistence.
instructions: Describe renderer crash recovery and window show fallback behavior.
Describe startup sequence, single-instance behavior, deep link handling, and hide-on-close/background mode.
Describe ui-state.json persistence (window bounds, theme, recentCwds, managedProcessesEnabled).

pages.title: Managed Background Processes
pages.purpose: Long-running dev-server process management: process_* tools, service lifecycle, containment, output buffers, readiness, and the crash reaper.
instructions: Document the process_* tool surface, owner session scoping, and limits.
Explain command policy (blocked detach commands, LAN bind confirmation) and fail-closed containment.
Explain the reaper: POSIX process groups, journal, owner identity, and host restart gating.
Explain the start/stop/restart lifecycle, readiness, stdin, output cursors, and reaper journaling.

pages.title: Windows Managed Process Helper
pages.purpose: The Rust win32 helper binary: Job Object containment, two-phase start, owner watchdog, reaper modes, integrity verification, and the JSON frame protocol.
instructions: Explain Job Object creation, two-phase commit, owner-lost watchdog, and grace/force stop phases.
Explain integrity verification (manifest.json, sha256, build id, provenance) and replaceability checks.
Explain owner-mode vs reaper-mode protocols and the frame codec.
Mention platform support limits (Windows x64 only) and packaging gates.
